summary: A locking wand hits an open door. C zap.c:bhit calls lock.c:doorlock, closes and locks the door, then learns the wand when visible, which exercises Wisdom. JavaScript bhit skips the doorlock call, so the unchanged door and missing identification cause the reported screen and RNG divergence; attrib.c:exercise is the downstream symptom.

source.branch: lock.c:doorlock (1102-1273) handles locking, opening, striking, and corresponding spells on secret or ordinary doors; it consumes lock.c:obstructed (926-953). The v11 case reaches the open-door WAN_LOCKING arm. zap.c:bhit (4059-4076) consumes doorlock return to decide learnwand and shop damage. muse.c:mbhit (1792 onward) consumes the same helper return for monster striking-wand behavior.
callers: zap.c:bhit calls doorlock for opening, locking, striking, knock, wizard lock, and force bolt when a wand ray meets a door; on true, it learns a visible wand and may bill a broken shop door. js/zap.js:bhit currently has no equivalent door arm.
muse.c:mbhit calls doorlock for monster WAN_OPENING, WAN_LOCKING, and WAN_STRIKING, then makes a seen wand known and records shop repair; js/muse.js currently records note_unported(lock.c doorlock).
lock.c:doorlock calls obstructed before locking a normal or Rogue doorway; the existing js/lock.js:obstructed has a visible-monster refusal and must be completed for the consumed Boolean.
dependencies: Preserve source door typ and doormask updates, message and vision ordering, blocked-square behavior, trapped-door consequences, shop damage, and picking cancellation. Complete the current partial js/lock.js:obstructed function and source name/map-invisible behavior.

The existing helpers cover block_point, unblock_point, recalc_block_point, cansee, map_invisible, picking_at, stop_occupation, reset_pick, in_rooms, and learnwand. Check each caller and return-value dependency against C.

The C-discarded trap.c:mb_trapped result and shk.c:add_damage effect require source review; only retain explicit note_unported for void calls still unported. Do not introduce a case-specific wand or door branch.

Independent C recipes should cover a distinct seeded open-door WAN_LOCKING outcome and SPE_WIZARD_LOCK through zap.c; seek a monster WAN_STRIKING door replay for the muse.c caller. Keep the v11 case as admitted-prefix evidence, not a copied regression recording.

evidence: Saved challenges/evaluations/20260928234726-v11.json at b8414122a83c8057895ab04b23b7f5c6876b3328 has 1 unmatched screen; C and JS match their first Wisdom exercise and its rn1(8,6) range draw, then C draws rn2(19)=8 at attrib.c:exercise after the door lock and wand discovery while JS enters later movement RNG. The first mismatch is at zero-based step 42.

The immutable C recording is challenges/cases/v11/wand-locking-closes-open-door.session.json (SHA-256 162cee8fb369b8f62557b3a80e460e4bb7da884869faf729efaa46d51827b30c); upstream zap.c:4059-4076 and lock.c:1102-1273 trace the successful door effect and learning.

Upstream lock.c:926-953 defines the Boolean obstruction helper and muse.c:1792 onward consumes doorlock for monster wand rays. js/lock.js:1311-1324 refuses a visible monster, js/muse.js:2380-2383 skips doorlock, and js/zap.js lacks the call.
